quest.title: Echoes of the Ancient World
quest.description: Help Verenata give the potions she has made to Carabosse. They appear to be conducting some music-related experiment...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x250, Primogem x30, Mora x20000, Hero's Wit x2, Mystic Enhancement Ore x3, Strange Part x1

dialogues.speaker: Verenata
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, and... and Paimon! We meet again!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, Verenata, it's been a while!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What are you doing here? Don't tell Paimon that you've crafted some new potion and are looking for more guinea pigs!

dialogues.speaker: Verenata
dialogues.text: No, no, that's not it... Actually, we've found a Melusine who's willing to help test that potion. Carabosse herself has already headed over to thoroughly document the potion's efficacy. It's just...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What?

dialogues.speaker: Verenata
dialogues.text: It's just... that Carabosse was so excited to hear that someone's willing to test it that she left home without bringing the potion...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Carabosse? Isn't she the great potioneer that you mentioned last time?

dialogues.speaker: Verenata
dialogues.text: #That's right! Thanks to {NICKNAME}'s help in testing our potions last time, we've gathered quite some data and information, with which the Master Potioneer managed to modify the formulae.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But didn't you tell us that no one's really willing to help the test because those potions aren't used to cure diseases?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It's kinda strange that someone's willing to do tests for you... Could it be that this Melusine secretly enjoys drinking strange stuff...?

dialogues.speaker: Verenata
dialogues.text: N—No! The Melusine in question is named Topyas.

dialogues.speaker: Verenata
dialogues.text: She claims to be a musician and volunteered when she heard that the Master Potioneer had developed some wondrous potion.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? That makes even less sense to Paimon! Why would a musician be interested in a potion?

choices.text: Perhaps it's a potion that can boost her musical talent.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon doesn't think Melusines usually take shortcuts like that though...

response.speaker: Verenata
response.text: T—To be honest, I don't know the details either.

response.speaker: Verenata
response.text: But Carabosse once said that potions and music are essentially connected, given that they both serve to manifest "truth."

response.speaker: Verenata
response.text: Oh, yes! Speaking of that, do you still remember the Truesight Potion I got you to test previously?

response.speaker: Verenata
response.text: We're bringing Topyas the enhanced version of that potion. The Master Potioneer seems to be really pleased with its modified formula.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #The enhanced version? The Truesight Potion {NICKNAME} tested was already strange enough. The effects of the enhanced version might be even worse, y'know!

response.speaker: Verenata
response.text: A—Anyway, can I ask you two for one more favor? I still have to gather lots and lots of herbs before the Master Potioneer returns.

response.speaker: Verenata
response.text: So I can only ask you two to take this potion to her... She should be with Topyas at the moment.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh! So it sounds like we just need to bring this potion over then? That seems easy enough...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: And this time, we'll finally meet that Master Potioneer!

choices.text: I'm quite interested in the potion, actually.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah! Maybe there's even a potion that helps you find hidden treasure! Just think of the Mora we'd make!

response.speaker: Verenata
response.text: Um, thank you so much for taking the potion to the Master Potioneer!

choices.text: Perhaps we'll be meeting someone dangerous.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: All the more reason to go take a look! It sure does seem like Melusines can't be poisoned, but if they drink enough weird potions, they still might have some strange reactions.

choices.text: Perhaps it's a potion that can help relieve fatigue.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That sounds about right! Musicians must feel really exhausted delving into music composition day after day!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, if there really is such a potion, Paimon thinks we need it too!

dialogues.speaker: Topyas
dialogues.text: Wololo... So many moons... One, two, three...

dialogues.speaker: Topyas
dialogues.text: Wololo... The stars are dancing... Wololo...

dialogues.speaker: Carabosse
dialogues.text: What the... I don't understand what you said at all! It seems that the "truth" shall remain elusive without the use of our latest potion, after all.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? So I guess this is the Master Potioneer we've heard so much about. She looks exceptionally ordinary to Paimon, though.

dialogues.speaker: Carabosse
dialogues.text: Oh? And who are you? It sounds like you're looking for me, specifically.

dialogues.speaker: Carabosse
dialogues.text: Humans attracted by my fame... I never realized my reputation as a potioneer had already spread so far among humankind...

dialogues.speaker: Carabosse
dialogues.text: *cough* Though as you can see, I am in the middle of an important experiment. If you desire a potion of my formulation, I must ask you to wait a bit longer.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Okay, that's not it at all... But you're right to say that we're looking for you... Verenata asked us to bring you this...

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You give the enhanced Truesight Potion to Carabosse.

dialogues.speaker: Carabosse
dialogues.text: Ooh la la, you've done me a great favor, haha! To be honest, I'd forgotten to bring this improved version of the Truesight Potion — and that left me at quite the loss!

dialogues.speaker: Carabosse
dialogues.text: Speaking of which, I do not believe I have yet learned your names, dear benefactors.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Paimon's Paimon, and {M#he's}{F#she's} {NICKNAME}.

dialogues.speaker: Carabosse
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}... Could you be the one who assisted with testing potions before? I recall seeing your name in Verenata's notes.

choices.text: In the flesh.

response.speaker: Carabosse
response.text: Haha, well, it is thanks to your previous assistance that I was able to use her precious notes to create an improved version.

response.speaker: Carabosse
response.text: And thus, it is clear that I owe you both a debt of gratitude. Should you require any potions, please, just tell me! No need to be polite!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: In that case, a potion that can make Mora out of... Wait! That's not what we're here for!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's Topyas, right? It seems like she's gone all loopy. Is she really okay?

response.speaker: Carabosse
response.text: Oh, that! You needn't worry. We Melusines are quite hardy, and won't be in any danger just from drinking something odd.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Um, you just straight up admitted that your potions are strange, didn't you?

response.speaker: Carabosse
response.text: In addition, in order to prevent any issues from popping up during the experiment, I specially concocted this "Pick-Me-Up Potion" to neutralize the effects. Using it should allow Topyas to immediately return to normal.

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: Carabosse administers the "Pick-Me-Up Potion" to Topyas, who quickly becomes more lucid.

response.speaker: Topyas
response.text: Wololo... Now, that felt like a very long time... Whoa, strangers! Haven't seen you around before!

response.speaker: Carabosse
response.text: #Well, now! Let me introduce them. These two are Paimon and {NICKNAME}. They are my benefactors. They were potion-testers previously.

response.speaker: Topyas
response.text: Oh, I see now... Hello, I'm Topyas, a musician from Merusea Village!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hehe, hiya there, Topyas!

response.speaker: Carabosse
response.text: It was also they who helped deliver the new formulation to me this time.

response.speaker: Carabosse
response.text: With this, we can begin the final experiment... The experiment that will grant us insight into the "truth."

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Um, Paimon's been really curious for a while now, but... Why would Topyas want to try this potion that supposedly lets you see the "truth"?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Though {NICKNAME} tried it before, all {M#he}{F#she} saw was this really weird "ghost ship"...

response.speaker: Topyas
response.text: Well, how should I put it... The essence of my music is an attempt to reveal the "truth" hidden all around us — things we usually don't see.

response.speaker: Topyas
response.text: Like the whisper of the waves, the call of sea stars, and joyous choruses of the sands...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Err, what? Paimon understands this less the more you go on...

response.speaker: Topyas
response.text: Anyway, it functions on the same principle as Carabosse's "Truesight Potion"!

response.speaker: Topyas
response.text: I had hoped to create music that could transmit the "truth" by my own strength, but...

response.speaker: Topyas
response.text: But I really don't have much time to prepare, and I want to give Mamere her gift as soon as possible...

response.speaker: Topyas
response.text: If I can't create a wonderful song quickly enough, then Mamere might leave the village again before it's ready!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh! So it's a gift for Mamere!

response.speaker: Topyas
response.text: Eh? You know her too?

choices.text: We're friends of hers.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's right! We're totally adventuring companions!

response.speaker: Topyas
response.text: Wooow! Since you're Mamere's partners, you must be really reliable!

response.speaker: Topyas
response.text: With your help, maybe I could get that thing...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What thing?

response.speaker: Topyas
response.text: Well, legend says that under the waters here, within a sealed ancient cave, lies the score upon which the "Melody of Vesta" is recorded.

response.speaker: Topyas
response.text: Though no Melusine has ever successfully entered the cave and retrieved the score, I've heard that when that melody is played, the listeners will be transported into a fantastical dreamland...

response.speaker: Topyas
response.text: So if we could obtain it, then I could still perform a song for Mamere as a gift, even without the "Truesight Potion"!

response.speaker: Carabosse
response.text: But there won't be anyone to help me test potions then...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait a minute, hold it! Didn't Topyas say that the music score was hidden in some sealed underwater cave?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: We've opened up a lot of seals in our time, sure, but if all we have to go on is some vague legend, this could be a long shot...

response.speaker: Topyas
response.text: That's true... But even so, can I ask you to at least accompany me to look at the seal? I'll definitely pay you!

response.speaker: Topyas
response.text: After all, you're Mamere's adventuring companions! Once you see that seal, I'm sure you'll definitely find a way to open it!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh... Well, if you put it like that, maybe we can at least go with you and take a look.

choices.text: Well, we are getting paid.

response.speaker: Carabosse
response.text: How very interesting! Why, I think I'll come along.

choices.text: As long as it's just a look.
We are adventuring companions.
Could be a case of "name's the same," for all you know...

response.speaker: Carabosse
response.text: Hmm. I strongly doubt anyone else in the world would share such a strange name. It must have been you, or I'm not Carabosse!

dialogues.speaker: Topyas
dialogues.text: We've arrived! This is it! If we enter through here, we'll reach the cave where the legendary lost music is hidden!

dialogues.speaker: Topyas
dialogues.text: I've heard that the humans who lived here hid it inside, long, long ago.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Um, it's just a legend, isn't it? You said that nobody's ever been inside, right? Maybe someone just saw the seal here and made up a legend about it...

dialogues.speaker: Topyas
dialogues.text: I guess that might be possible... No, wait! This is a really ancient legend, and I heard it when I was young! There's no way it could be fake!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, this seal looks pretty ordinary! And since it's here, there's gotta be a mechanism that opens it! Let's look around.

dialogues.speaker: Topyas
dialogues.text: Don't bother! I've looked all over this area here countless times, and there's nothing that looks even vaguely like a mechanism.

dialogues.speaker: Topyas
dialogues.text: And if there really was, then it would have been discovered ages ago, instead of nobody being able to get inside...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Well, if there are no mechanisms around, even {NICKNAME} wouldn't be able to break the seal... Could someone have hidden them in some way that no one can find them?

dialogues.speaker: Carabosse
dialogues.text: Oh, you mean some kind of invisible mechanism? Well, this seems like a job for yours truly.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Eh?

dialogues.speaker: Carabosse
dialogues.text: Have you already forgotten the "Truesight Potion" you brought me? It is a potion that allows one to see what cannot be seen.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? You mean anyone who drinks it will be able to see the mechanisms?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Well, {NICKNAME} did see some really weird stuff after drinking it before, but it doesn't seem all that reliable...

dialogues.speaker: Carabosse
dialogues.text: #Rest assured! Though I can't guarantee that it will work if a Melusine drinks it, things will certainly work out if {NICKNAME} does!

dialogues.speaker: Carabosse
dialogues.text: After all, this improved version is based upon the data we gained from the last time you tried it.

dialogues.speaker: Carabosse
dialogues.text: #So from a certain perspective, {NICKNAME} is the perfect test subject for this new version.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Baloney! You just want us to keep being your guinea pigs!

dialogues.speaker: Carabosse
dialogues.text: Ah, come now, this formula truly is my pride and joy. If there really is some mechanism that cannot be seen, you will definitely be able to see it if you drink this!

dialogues.speaker: Carabosse
dialogues.text: You've tried it once before, have you not? It can't hurt to have another go!

choices.text: A capital proposal.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Um... you should still be careful...

response.speaker: Carabosse
response.text: Then please, drink this Truesight Potion. I am looking forward to your feedback.

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: You take the Truesight Potion from Carabosse, and gulp it down before the pungent aroma has a chance to spread...\nJust like before, it seems not to taste like anything...

response.speaker: Carabosse
response.text: Good. The potion should be taking effect by now. Try to see if you can find what we're looking for nearby.

choices.text: If we're just trying it...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Um... please be careful...

talks.objective: Look for a way to break the seal

dialogues.speaker: Verenata
dialogues.text: Um, I'll leave it to you to deliver the potion.

dialogues.speaker: Topyas
dialogues.text: The seal really opened... I didn't even see how you did it...

dialogues.speaker: Carabosse
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME} must have seen something we cannot, and done something to it.

choices.text: That's right...

response.speaker: Carabosse
response.text: Oho, what an excellent result! Something that only those who see the "truth" can interact with...

response.speaker: Carabosse
response.text: This "truth" is not bound to the confines of our own thoughts and eyes... It is different from ordinary subjective records. It is a completely reliable and objective record.

response.speaker: Carabosse
response.text: Though I cannot say if it is because of your innate talents or the potion, I believe the development of this Truesight Potion has certainly taken its first step towards success.

response.speaker: Carabosse
response.text: Next, we must figure out the underlying principles behind the potion's effects, and continue to improve it...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh!? You don't even understand the basic principles behind how it works and asked us to test it anyway? That's way too irresponsible!

response.speaker: Carabosse
response.text: Haha, what can I say? Potioneering is an experimental science! Practical results are more important than principles and theory!

response.speaker: Carabosse
response.text: Without experimentation, even I have no way to possibly confirm its effects!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ugh, then Paimon has no idea what to say... But ignoring the potions for now, at least we can finally enter the cave!

response.speaker: Topyas
response.text: True... The lost musical score of the "Melody of Vesta" should be inside. Let's hurry in and look!

response.speaker: Carabosse
response.text: Ah, though I am also quite interested in this legendary lost music... Now that I have received new feedback concerning the Truesight Potion, I should go back and work on its next iteration.

response.speaker: Carabosse
response.text: As such, I shall be taking my leave for now. My thanks, benefactors.

response.speaker: Carabosse
response.text: Remember, if there are any other potions you'd like to try in the future, come and find me.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmm... Anyway, since the seal is open, let's go in and have a look! Maybe we'll find something unexpected!

choices.text: It was a pretty normal mechanism.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: After Topyas makes some last-minute adjustments to the components on the conch, she begins the conch harp performance...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow, what wonderful music... Even though it took so long, Paimon knew it wasn't all for nothing the instant she heard it!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It washed away all our fatigue, just like that!

dialogues.speaker: Topyas
dialogues.text: Yes! Even though it can't carry people off into a dreamscape like the legend says, it is truly beautiful music.

dialogues.speaker: Topyas
dialogues.text: It's definitely good enough to be a parting gift for Mamere!

dialogues.speaker: Topyas
dialogues.text: Thank you both so much! You both spent so much time running around and worked so hard for the sake of my music...

choices.text: After all, we're Mamere's companions.

response.speaker: Topyas
response.text: Anyway, I'm so grateful! Thank you!

response.speaker: Topyas
response.text: Oh, right! And this is the reward I promised you.

response.speaker: Topyas
response.text: If you have time, please come back and listen to more beautiful music!

choices.text: No worries. We're used to it.

dialogues.speaker: Carabosse
dialogues.text: The potion should have taken effect. Do you notice anything different?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I see crystal devices I couldn't before.

dialogues.speaker: Carabosse
dialogues.text: Huh, guess the new recipe works! Well, try touching them. Let's see what happens!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Here we are! Now let's look at the score we just found!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Just what kind of music has it recorded? Paimon can't wait to find out!

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: After a quick cleanup, you present the lost musical score to Topyas.

dialogues.speaker: Topyas
dialogues.text: Mm...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Mm-hmm...

dialogues.speaker: Topyas
dialogues.text: Yeah... Nope. I can't understand what this score says at all...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? But aren't you a musician, Topyas? You should have no trouble reading musical scores!

dialogues.speaker: Topyas
dialogues.text: Um... Though the bronze plate does have a musical score on it, I've never seen any of the symbols before.

dialogues.speaker: Topyas
dialogues.text: I've read lots of human notation before, but this is really the first time I've seen anything like this...

dialogues.speaker: Topyas
dialogues.text: Ohh, what am I going to do... If I can't understand this notation, then I won't be able to play a beautiful enough song for Mamere...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Come on, don't worry! Since it's a music score, there's definitely some way to read it!

choices.text: We just need to find someone who can understand it.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah! Since it's a lost ancient score, maybe it uses some kind of lost ancient language!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Anyway! It should be fine if we go and find Katheryne in the Court of Fontaine!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Fontaine is full of artists, and if the Adventurers' Guild helps us, we can definitely find someone who can read it.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Why don't you head back and wait for us, Topyas? Once we figure this thing out, we'll come find you!

response.speaker: Topyas
response.text: *sniff* ...Then I'll leave it to you!

choices.text: Some music scores just can't be read.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: If it's like that, then it probably doesn't count as a music score!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Long time no see, Katheryne!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm... It looks like you're busy! We'll wait over there.

dialogues.speaker: Katheryne
dialogues.text: It's fine. This young lady has almost finished settling her business.

dialogues.speaker: Katheryne
dialogues.text: Are you here for new commissions today?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, no, not this time! We're actually here to post one.

dialogues.speaker: Katheryne
dialogues.text: I never thought there would be a problem seasoned adventurers like yourselves couldn't solve. What is the commission you would like to post?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Actually...

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You explain the situation with the lost music score to Katheryne.

dialogues.speaker: Tailleferre
dialogues.text: Huh? It sounds like you're talking about music.

dialogues.speaker: Katheryne
dialogues.text: Oh! The young lady who was just here posting a commission is also a musician. Perhaps she may have some leads for you.

dialogues.speaker: Tailleferre
dialogues.text: Hello. My name is Tailleferre. Could I have a look at the score you mentioned just now?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Of course! If you can understand it, that'd be amazing!

dialogues.speaker: Tailleferre
dialogues.text: Let me see... Yes, this material, and this notation of phonetic notes... It is exactly as I thought! This is a score left behind by the ancient Remurians.

choices.text: Remurians?

response.speaker: Tailleferre
response.text: You've never heard of it? Remuria is the name of the ancient civilization that controlled these waters before the foundation of the Court of Fontaine.

response.speaker: Tailleferre
response.text: Phonetic notes were a writing system used by the Remurians, but rather than recording languages, they were used to record music.

response.speaker: Tailleferre
response.text: The civilization of the Remurians was based around music. It is said that they once built a massive musical instrument, even grander than our opera house, that was capable of playing music even to the dome of the sky.

response.speaker: Tailleferre
response.text: The legends say they sailed musical ships that could carry thousands, and that each sigh and shudder of every note was carried to the edges of their empire.

response.speaker: Tailleferre
response.text: But thousands of years ago, a great flood destroyed all of this in a single day. The civilization of Remuria also perished in that cataclysmic tide.

response.speaker: Tailleferre
response.text: But though the civilization of Remuria vanished, they left behind a rich legacy for Fontaine.

response.speaker: Tailleferre
response.text: Especially in the arts. Whether in music, drawing, or sculpture, we have all been deeply influenced by the Remurian civilization. It would not be exaggerating to say that they are the font of all the arts in Fontaine.

response.speaker: Tailleferre
response.text: Not to mention one of the greatest musicians in Fontaine's history — Boethius. He himself served as the Harmost for the court of Remuria itself.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, since you obviously knew enough to give that whole speech, then you should have no problem reading the score, right?

response.speaker: Tailleferre
response.text: Oh, sorry, I didn't realize I had gotten so far off topic...

response.speaker: Tailleferre
response.text: Any musician who wishes to attain greatness must study the musical theory left behind by Remuria.

response.speaker: Tailleferre
response.text: The "Melody of Vesta"... Though I've never seen the movements written here before, since it has been written using ordinary phonetic notes, it's not difficult at all to understand. But...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But? But what!? There isn't going to be some new problem to solve, is there?

response.speaker: Tailleferre
response.text: However, this music cannot be performed using ordinary instruments. Based on the arrangement of the phonetic symbols, it must have been written for a specific instrument.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh... So if we want to play this music, we'll have to find some kind of special instrument? This is getting more and more complicated...

response.speaker: Tailleferre
response.text: That's correct. I recall that according to legend, the Remurians would sometimes use a huge conch to perform music of this sort...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: A huge conch... Paimon feels like we've seen one somewhere before...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: There was one back where we ran into Topyas...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh! That's right! Maybe that thing really is...

response.speaker: Tailleferre
response.text: It looks like you two already have a lead! If you don't mind, I'll mark up the movements on the score for you. That way, anyone with even a basic sense of music theory should be able to understand it.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah! That would be great, thank you so much!

response.speaker: Katheryne
response.text: Since your problem has already been successfully resolved, I believe it will be unnecessary to post your commission. As for the reward, you can simply give it directly to this young lady.

response.speaker: Tailleferre
response.text: Haha, there's no need for a reward. Being able to see a score from Remuria that I've never seen before is reward enough for me.

response.speaker: Tailleferre
response.text: In that case, we'll see you later!

choices.text: "Phonetic notes"?

response.speaker: Tailleferre
response.text: You didn't know? Phonetic notes were a writing system used by the Remurians, but rather than recording languages, they were used to record music.

response.speaker: Tailleferre
response.text: Remuria is the name of the ancient civilization that controlled these waters before the foundation of the Court of Fontaine.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, Topyas, we're baaack!

dialogues.speaker: Topyas
dialogues.text: #Oh! It's you, {NICKNAME}, Paimon.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hehe, we've figured the music out!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But before we talk about that, there's something we want to ask you!

choices.text: About the giant conch we saw...

response.speaker: Topyas
response.text: Oh! If you're asking about conch harps, then yes, that is indeed an instrument.

response.speaker: Topyas
response.text: In fact, it's the first instrument I learned to play!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Then it looks like we were right on the Mora! See...

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: You give the annotated copy of the "Melody of Vesta" to Topyas, and then you tell her about the lost score and the conch harp, which Tailleferre mentioned.

response.speaker: Topyas
response.text: Oh! Now I understand. So this music was originally written to be played by a conch harp...

response.speaker: Topyas
response.text: To tell the truth, if it weren't for the conch harp, I wouldn't even have any interest in music... My first memories of this world are all of the conch harp...

response.speaker: Topyas
response.text: As for why, well, it's because my token is the component used to play conch harps, of course!

response.speaker: Topyas
response.text: But perhaps it's because the sound of conch harps is a bit too unique, or maintaining them is too complicated... I would always attract a bunch of strange creatures whenever I played it.

response.speaker: Topyas
response.text: At some point, I just... stopped using it to play music.

response.speaker: Topyas
response.text: #{NICKNAME}, will you help me clean up the conch harp?

response.speaker: Topyas
response.text: All we need to do is place this token and clean up the conch's mouthpiece!

response.speaker: Topyas
response.text: Then, we just need to adjust the token, and then we can start playing!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh! So we just need to put it in, then? That's a piece of cake! Let's go over together!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hehe, Paimon's really looking forward to this! Paimon wonders just what kind of music we're gonna get...

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: You and Topyas arrive near the conch harp...

choices.text: About conch-like instruments...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: If that's the case, then why don't you study the score here, Topyas? We'll go place your token in the meantime!

dialogues.speaker: Topyas
dialogues.text: It's been so long... Would anything else have gone wrong with the harp in the meantime?

dialogues.speaker: Topyas
dialogues.text: Anyway, I'm counting on you!

talks.objective: Use the Xenochromatic Armored Crab's ability to unleash shockwaves at the Conch Harp
Clear out the creatures dwelling within the Conch Harp

dialogues.speaker: Topyas
dialogues.text: After drinking this potion, can you really see anything you couldn't before?

dialogues.speaker: Topyas
dialogues.text: If you can see any mechanisms you couldn't before, then you should be able to open up the seal...

dialogues.speaker: Topyas
dialogues.text: *sniff* Then I'll leave the music in your hands...

dialogues.speaker: Topyas
dialogues.text: Hey, it's easy to understand the score now!

dialogues.speaker: Topyas
dialogues.text: As long as we adjust the components properly, then we can play the conch harp!
